subject: Usuing UI elements created inside a Shiny Module

messages.author: 791c159e9fcbd222
messages.subject: Usuing UI elements created inside a Shiny Module
parts:
I cannot seem to access the results of a radiobutton that is dynamically generated in a Shiny Module UI.  In the simple example included (thanks to Barbara Borges) I try to simply print the choice made when selecting a radiobutton for input question 1 and display that choice in the output tab.  The app seems to believe that the input (input$id) is null:


# ------------------------------------ MODULE ----------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# module UI
modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
 
  tagList(
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc01"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
   
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc02"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
   
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc03"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
   
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc04"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:", choices = c(""))
  )
}

# module server
mod <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {
 
  createLabel <- function(name) {
    paste0(name, ": ",
           questionSet[questionSet$QID == name,]$Element.Question,
           sep = "")
  }
 
  output$labelQc01 <- renderText({ createLabel("C01") })
  output$labelQc02 <- renderText({ createLabel("C02") })
  output$labelQc03 <- renderText({ createLabel("C03") })
  output$labelQc04 <- renderText({ createLabel("C04") })
 
  createOptions <- function(row) {
    as.character(questionSet[row,5:ncol(questionSet)])
  }
 
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c1", choices = createOptions(1))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c2", choices = createOptions(2))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c3", choices = createOptions(3))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c4", choices = createOptions(4))
}

# ----------------------------------- MAIN APP ---------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)

questionSet <- tibble::tibble(
  QID = c("C01", "C02", "C03", "C04"),
  Element.Question = c(
    "Do you like icecream?",
    "Do you like sunny days?",
    "Do you like going to the movies?",
    "Do you like coffee?"
  ),
  col3 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  col4 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  Option1 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  Option2 = c("No", "No", "No", "No"),
  Option3 = c("Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe")
)

ui <- navbarPage("Select:",
                 tabPanel("Inputs", modUI("questions")),
                 tabPanel("Outputs",
                          textOutput("testthis"),
                          textOutput("testthat"),
                          verbatimTextOutput("debug")
)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  callModule(mod, "questions", questionSet = questionSet)
  output$testthis <- renderText({1:17})
  output$testthat <- renderText(ifelse(is.null(input$ns("c3")),"This IS NULL",input$ns("c3")))
#  print(output$testthis))

output$debug <- renderPrint({
  input$c1
})


}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.author: d6ebe55625e8e5a2
messages.subject: Re: Usuing UI elements created inside a Shiny Module
parts:
This is by design. From the modules article:

 The input, output, and session objects we’re provided with are special, in that they are scoped to the specific namespace that matches up with our UI function. 

 

On the flip side, the input, output, and session cannot be used to access inputs/outputs that are outside of the namespace, nor can they directly access reactive expressions and reactive values from elsewhere in the application (OK, technically, lexically scoped reactive expressions/values can be used, but that’s it ). 

 

These restrictions are by design, and they are important. The goal is not to prevent modules from interacting with their containing apps, but rather, to make these interactions explicit. If a module needs to use a reactive expression, take the reactive expression as a function parameter. If a module wants to return reactive expressions to the calling app, then return a list of reactive expressions from the function.


As the last sentence makes clear, you need to return the values that you may want to use on the main app (though you should strive to keep the code encapsulated in the module itself as much as possible). Here's what it would look like in your example (taking away the unnecessary outputs and tabPanels for ease of visualization):

# ------------------------------------ MODULE ----------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# module UI
modUI <- function(id) {
  ns <- NS(id)
  
  tagList(
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc01"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c1"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
    
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc02"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c2"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
    
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc03"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c3"), "Please Select:", choices = c("")),
    tags$hr(style = "border-color: darkblue;"),
    
    h4(textOutput(ns("labelQc04"))),
    radioButtons(ns("c4"), "Please Select:", choices = c(""))
  )
}

# module server
mod <- function(input, output, session, questionSet) {
  
  createLabel <- function(name) {
    paste0(name, ": ", 
      questionSet[questionSet$QID == name,]$Element.Question,
      sep = "")
  }
  
  output$labelQc01 <- renderText({ createLabel("C01") })
  output$labelQc02 <- renderText({ createLabel("C02") })
  output$labelQc03 <- renderText({ createLabel("C03") })
  output$labelQc04 <- renderText({ createLabel("C04") })
  
  createOptions <- function(row) {
    as.character(questionSet[row,5:ncol(questionSet)])
  }
  
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c1", choices = createOptions(1))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c2", choices = createOptions(2))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c3", choices = createOptions(3))
  updateRadioButtons(session, "c4", choices = createOptions(4))

return(list(
    c1 = reactive(input$c1), 
    c2 = reactive(input$c2), 
    c3 = reactive(input$c3), 
    c4 = reactive(input$c4)

))
}

# ----------------------------------- MAIN APP ---------------------------------
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny)

questionSet <- tibble::tibble(
  QID = c("C01", "C02", "C03", "C04"),
  Element.Question = c(
    "Do you like icecream?",
    "Do you like sunny days?",
    "Do you like going to the movies?",
    "Do you like coffee?"
  ),
  col3 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  col4 = c(character(1), character(1), character(1), character(1)),
  Option1 = c("Yes", "Yes", "Yes", "Yes"),
  Option2 = c("No", "No", "No", "No"),
  Option3 = c("Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe", "Maybe")
)

results <- callModule(mod, "questions", questionSet = questionSet)
  
  output$answers <- renderUI({
    tagList(
      h4("Answers from module, displayed from main app"),
      div(strong("c1"), " answer: ", results$c1()),
      div(strong("c2"), " answer: ", results$c2()),
      div(strong("c3"), " answer: ", results$c3()),
      div(strong("c4"), " answer: ", results$c4())
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
